sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Robertson County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Two elected offices in Springfield split the work. The Assessor of Property values the land and buildings, and the County Trustee bills and collects the money. The Register of Deeds records the paperwork that connects the two when a house changes hands.

  • Assessor of Property: Chris Traughber, 521 S. Brown St., Springfield, 615-384-4311, weekday hours 8 to 4:30.
  • County Trustee: Kendra Shelton, Room 161 of the Robertson County Office Building, 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, Monday through Friday until 4:30 p.m.
  • Register of Deeds: John West, same weekday schedule.

The trustee reported that in 2025 the office collected about $60 million in property tax payments on more than 40,000 parcels. Anyone selling a home here is dealing with a system built for volume, so ask for written payoff figures instead of relying on a phone estimate.

sections.h2: What does a seller in Robertson County need to know about the local housing market?
sections.html:
Robertson County sits on the Kentucky line and belongs to the Nashville metropolitan area. The Census Bureau estimated 80,175 residents on July 1, 2025, up 10.1 percent from the 2020 base of 72,809.

Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $335,000, with median household income of $83,047 and a 77.6 percent owner-occupancy rate. Median gross rent is $1,199, which is lower than neighboring Rutherford County. The county covers 476.34 square miles of land, so density is only 152.8 people per square mile.

Springfield is the county seat. Other incorporated places include Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier, Orlinda, Coopertown, Ridgetop and White House, while Millersville and Portland sit mainly in Sumner County. Interstate 65 follows the eastern border for about 20 miles, and Interstate 24 runs along the southwestern border for about 10 miles.

sections.h2: What is the Robertson County tax calendar, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
Bills are payable from the first Monday in October through the last day of February without penalty. Starting March 1, the state adds 1.5 percent interest to the unpaid balance, and another 1.5 percent on the first of each month after that.

Robertson County real property tax calendar
StepWhat happensSource
January 1Owner on this date carries tax liability for the tax yearCounty Trustee
First Monday of OctoberTaxes become payable; notices go out in early October when the commission has set the rateCounty Trustee
Last day of FebruaryFinal day to pay without interest (Friday, February 27 for the 2025 bill)County Trustee
March 11.5% interest begins, T.C.A. 67-5-2010County Trustee
March 15Last day to pay a year-delinquent bill at the trustee officeCounty Trustee
March 16 to 31Delinquent real property goes to the tax attorney, then a Chancery Court suit, T.C.A. 67-5-2404County Trustee

The 2025 deadline of February 27, 2026 has passed. The 2026 bill follows the same pattern, so ask the trustee for the final in-office day if the 28th lands on a Saturday or Sunday.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Robertson County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail, online, by phone, or through your bank draft. Partial payments and prepayments are allowed while the bill is still in the trustee office.

  • In person: Room 161 of the county office building during office hours, or the drop box by the sliding front door.
  • Drive thru: a kiosk lane at the office building.
  • Local banks: The Farmers Bank (all branches) and United Community Bank in Springfield, current year only and October through February, with the paper notice in hand.
  • Online or phone: tnproptax.com or 1-877-556-4079. The vendor charges 2.50 percent on cards or $1.25 on e-checks, plus $0.30 for phone payments, and the county keeps none of it.
  • Mail: the postmark date counts for interest.
  • Auto draft: monthly on the 10th, with the enrollment form received before the first of the prior month.

Most mortgage servicers pay in December, and the trustee suggests checking tnproptax.com to confirm the payment posted before the March 1 cutoff.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Robertson County house is sold mid-year?
sections.html:
The trustee says the owner as of January 1 is responsible for that year's bill, and the contract between buyer and seller can shift the cost between them. The trustee's office keeps no record of those contracts, so the burden of checking falls on you.

The Assessor adds a timing detail. After the Register of Deeds records a deed, the Assessor receives a copy the next day, and moving the parcel into the buyer's name takes roughly 90 days. The bill goes to whatever name was on file January 1 until the following year, and the closing papers should say who pays. Tax notices are not mailed to the mortgage company.

A practical step for sellers: before closing, ask the trustee for a current balance on every parcel you own. The trustee warns that deeds are indexed under different spellings of a name, so a search by name alone can miss a parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Robertson County assessment?
sections.html:
The path runs from the Assessor's office to the local equalization board and then to the state board. Tennessee's Appeals Handbook says county boards normally convene on June 1 and sit as long as the volume of appeals requires.

A taxpayer who disagrees with the county board can appeal to the state board by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date the local board's notice was sent, whichever is later (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). The state may charge up to $10 for processing an appeal. The assessment date is January 1 of the tax year, so events after that date are generally irrelevant to the value, and the handbook treats recent comparable sales as the strongest evidence of a house's value.

Look up your parcel, owner name or address on the state-maintained Tennessee Property Data site that the Assessor links to, then compare the card against what you know about the house.

sections.h2: What relief and special programs does the Robertson County Trustee run?
sections.html:
The trustee's page lists three programs for eligible owners: a Tax Relief Program, a Tax Freeze Program and a Wheel Tax Rebate. In 2025 the office reported roughly 950 people in the freeze program, about 1,200 in the relief program and about 135 wheel tax rebates.

Farmland owners should also know about greenbelt. The Assessor mails greenbelt applications within 90 days of a processed deed. If land leaves agricultural, forest or open space use, rollback taxes apply: the difference between use value and market value for the preceding three years for farm and forest land, or five years for open space. They are not a penalty and become delinquent March 15 of the following year (T.C.A. 67-5-1008(d)). Anyone selling acreage should ask the Assessor whether a change of use is coming.

sections.h2: What if I want to sell a Robertson County house with tax still due?
sections.html:
You can sell with taxes unpaid, because the balance is settled from the sale proceeds. A buyer, lender or title company will want the number, so get it from the trustee in writing.

Timing changes the process. While a real property bill is under one year delinquent, it stays with the trustee, who accepts partial payments. Once it is turned over, payment goes through Robertson County Chancery Court at 615-384-5650 and extra costs attach. Delinquent personal property tax for 2015 through 2024 can be paid through American Financial Credit Services at 888-317-2327 extension 3.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, but you should still compare the payoff against the offer. Ask the title company to show the trustee payoff as its own line on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: What is the Robertson County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The last day of February without interest. For the 2025 bill the final day was Friday, February 27, 2026. Interest of 1.5 percent starts March 1 and repeats on the first of each following month.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Robertson County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Trustee's office in Room 161 of the county office building at 515 S. Brown St. in Springfield, at the drop box or drive thru, at local banks listed by the trustee, online at tnproptax.com, or by mail.

faqs.q: How long does a deed take to show up with the Robertson County Assessor?
faqs.a: About 90 days. The Assessor gets a copy the day after recording, then moves the parcel into the new owner's name. The tax bill goes to the January 1 owner until the next year.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Robertson County assessment after the county board meets?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the State Board of Equalization by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. Ask the Assessor at 615-384-4311 for the county step first.

faqs.q: Does Robertson County have a property tax relief program for seniors?
faqs.a: The Trustee runs a Tax Relief Program and a Tax Freeze Program. Call 615-384-4238 for eligibility rules and application timing, because the trustee sets the current requirements.
